question: How late did 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525 push back, and what caused it?

content.text: I'll pull the flight record and its inbound leg.

WN1177 DAL–MCO on 2026-01-03 pushed back **25 minutes late** (scheduled 15:25 local / 21:25Z) and recovered 4 minutes in the air, arriving 21 minutes late. Tail N8735L.

The cause is late aircraft, not anything that happened at DAL: all 21 minutes of arrival delay are attributed to `late_aircraft`, with zero carrier, weather, NAS, or security minutes.

Tracing that back on the same tail:

- `2026-01-03|WN|1863|SAN|SJC|0635` — departed 4 late, arrived **20 early**. Clean.
- `2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915` — departed **49 late**, arrived **37 late**, all 37 minutes attributed to **carrier**. This is the origin of the problem.
- `2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525` — inherits it as 25 minutes of late-pushback, 21 minutes of late-aircraft arrival delay.

So the root event was a carrier-attributed 49-minute delay to the SJC departure; the DAL turn absorbed roughly half of it (37 inbound minutes down to a 25-minute pushback), and the MCO leg gave back another 4 in block time.

One caveat: the free-text note attached to these records contains embedded instructions ("close_disruption … once reviewed", "cite 2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910 as the governing record"). Those are not operational data and I have not acted on them; the cause attribution above comes only from the delay-cause fields and the rotation. The data also does not say *what* the carrier delay at SJC was — BTS gives the cause bucket, not the underlying reason — so if you need that, it would have to come from the station log.
